subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging IGCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Cambridge spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: In a flowchart, which symbol shape is used to represent a decision?
questions.explain: A diamond represents a decision with a condition and typically two exit paths (yes/no). Rectangles are processes, parallelograms are input/output, ovals are start/stop.

questions.q: In Cambridge pseudocode, which line correctly assigns the value 10 to a variable named Count?
questions.explain: Cambridge pseudocode uses the left arrow <- for assignment, so Count <- 10 is correct. A single = is used only for comparison.

questions.q: Which Cambridge pseudocode data type would best store the value 3.14?
questions.explain: REAL stores numbers with a fractional/decimal part. INTEGER stores whole numbers only, CHAR a single character, BOOLEAN a TRUE/FALSE value.

questions.q: A program stores whether a user is logged in as either TRUE or FALSE. Which data type is most appropriate?
questions.explain: A BOOLEAN holds only TRUE or FALSE, which exactly matches a two-state login flag.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a variable and a constant?
options: A constant can change value; a variable cannot
A variable can change value during execution; a constant keeps the same value throughout
questions.explain: A variable's value can change while the program runs. A constant is assigned once and its value stays fixed, e.g. CONSTANT Pi = 3.142.

questions.q: A FOR ... NEXT loop is an example of which programming construct?
questions.explain: A FOR loop repeats a fixed number of times based on a counter, making it count-controlled iteration. A WHILE loop is condition-controlled.

questions.q: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once because the condition is tested at the end?
questions.explain: REPEAT ... UNTIL checks the condition after running the body, so the body always runs at least once. A WHILE loop checks first and may run zero times.

questions.q: In Cambridge pseudocode, what does the expression 17 MOD 5 evaluate to?
questions.explain: MOD returns the remainder of integer division. 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so 17 MOD 5 = 2. (17 DIV 5 would be 3.)

questions.q: Which condition is TRUE only when BOTH X > 5 AND Y < 3 are satisfied?
questions.explain: The AND (logical) operator requires both operands to be TRUE for the whole expression to be TRUE. OR only needs one.

questions.q: Which Cambridge pseudocode statement correctly declares a 1D array of 10 integers indexed 1 to 10?
questions.explain: Cambridge pseudocode declares arrays with lower and upper bounds: DECLARE Numbers : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER.

questions.q: A 2D array is best suited to storing which of the following?
options: Data arranged in rows and columns, such as a grid or table
questions.explain: A 2D array uses two indices (row and column), making it ideal for table/grid-like data such as a seating plan or spreadsheet.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a procedure and a function in Cambridge pseudocode?
options: A function returns a single value; a procedure does not return a value
A procedure returns a value; a function does not
Functions cannot be called more than once
questions.explain: A function returns a single value to the point where it was called (using RETURN). A procedure carries out a task but does not return a value.

questions.q: What is a parameter in a subroutine?
options: A value returned to the main program
A value passed into the subroutine when it is called
questions.explain: A parameter is a value passed into a procedure or function when it is called, allowing the same subroutine to work with different data.

questions.q: Which Cambridge pseudocode library routine returns a random value?
questions.explain: RANDOM (or RAND) returns a random number. ROUND rounds a value, LENGTH gives string length, and INT/DIV handle integer conversion.

questions.q: If the string variable Word holds "COMPUTER", what does LENGTH(Word) return?
questions.explain: LENGTH returns the number of characters. "COMPUTER" has 8 characters, so LENGTH(Word) = 8.

questions.q: In Cambridge pseudocode, SUBSTRING or MID is used to extract part of a string. From "PROGRAM", extracting 3 characters starting at position 1 would give:
questions.explain: Starting at the first character and taking 3 characters gives "PRO".

questions.q: Which sequence of Cambridge pseudocode keywords correctly reads from a file?
options: OPENFILE ... FOR READ, then READFILE, then CLOSEFILE
OPENFILE ... FOR READ, then WRITEFILE, then ENDFILE
OPENFILE ... FOR WRITE, then WRITEFILE, then CLOSEFILE
questions.explain: To read, open the file for reading (OPENFILE FileName FOR READ), read data with READFILE, then CLOSEFILE when finished.

questions.q: A program checks that an entered age is between 0 and 120. What type of check is this?
questions.explain: A range check confirms a value falls within a set of allowed limits (here 0 to 120). A length check counts characters; a format check tests a pattern.

questions.q: Asking a user to type a password twice and comparing the two entries is an example of:
questions.explain: Verification checks that data has been entered/copied accurately. Double entry compares two inputs; validation instead checks whether data is reasonable/allowable.

questions.q: A loop runs: Total <- 0, then FOR i <- 1 TO 3, Total <- Total + i, NEXT i. Using a trace table, what is the final value of Total?
questions.explain: Tracing: i=1 gives Total 1; i=2 gives Total 3; i=3 gives Total 6. The final value is 6 (1+2+3).
